Commentary.Commentary: It was a mixed bag for New Zealand. They were up against some stupendous bowling and at the same time, didn't apply themselves well and threw their wickets away. Jeet Raval was the only one who stood tall and put up any kind of a fight. Everybody else, just crumbled when it counted. So, are we in for a 3-day finish? Remains to be seen. Don't go anywhere as the final innings of the match is about to start.

It would be an understatement to say that South Africa have their noses in front. They just need 81 runs to win this game. A spectacular bowling display from Keshav Maharaj has seen the Proteas run through the Kiwis batting order. The spinner bagged a 6-fer and ended with career best figures of 6/40. But, it was a collective bowling display from Faf du Plessis' men. It was first Morne Morkel to wreak havoc, grabbing 3 wickets, and then Rabada (1 wicket) and Philander bowled brutal spells, keeping the pressure on New Zealand throughout.

OUT! Maharaj gets his sixth! Tossed up around middle and leg, Watling dances down the track to reach the pitch of the ball. He does not get there well and only manages to uppishly drive this one towards the fielder at mid off. Duminy gets forward and takes a sitter. Maharaj also registers his career best figures of 20.2-7-6-40. NEW ZEALAND END ON 171!
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Good shot! Short and wide outside off, Wagner guides this one over the slip cordon for a boundary.
Short delivery into the body, Wagner somehow defends it towards the fielder at point off his gloves.
Full delivery into the stumps, Wagner defends it back to the bowler.
Neil Wagner is the last batsman to walk in for New Zealand.

OUT! Rabada gets his first! Short delivery into the body, Rabada goes for the pull but only manages to glove it. The ball flies away towards the keeper. Quinton takes an easy catch and appeals for it. The umpire raises his finger and Jeetan Patel has to walk back to the pavilion. South Africa only need 1 wicket to get back with the bat.
Another short ball into the body, Jeetan Patel stands tall and defends it off his handle.
Short delivery to start with, Patel ducks under it.
Full outside off, Watling drives this one towards the cover fielder.
Tossed up outside off, Watling prods forward and defends it.
Jeetan Patel is in to bat now.

OUT! Southee throws it away! On a length and spinning away, Southee lofts it over the mid off region. Seems like he was giving catching practice. Duminy the fielder there, gets under it and takes a regulation catch. Keshav Maharaj is having a day to remember. New Zealand are throwing it away.
Fuller delivery, Watling drives it for a single through mid off.
Southee drives it down the ground for a single through mid off.
Angling in from a length around off, Southee prods forward in defence and gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Angling into the stumps from a good length, Watling stays in his crease and defends it.
Dug in short this time, Watling ducks under it to let that go through to the keeper.
Length delivery outside off, Watling covers his stumps and lets it through to the keeper.
Short delivery into the batsman, Southee pulls it off his glove towards the fine leg region for a single.
Down the leg side, Watling nudges it fine for a single.
Watling stays deep in his crease to defend it.
Full delivery in the line of the stumps, Southee clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, Southee clips it through the mid-wicket region. The batsmen run a couple.
Short and wide outside off, Southee pushes it towards point.
Tim Southee walks into the middle next.

OUT! Castled! Tossed up around middle and leg, the ball spins a away a lot. Colin de Grandhomme goes deep in his crease and hangs his bat in defence. He is totally beaten by the away spin as it goes onto rattle the stumps. Another poor performance by the batsman. Maharaj is making the most of it.
Watling reaches the pitch of the ball and drives it through mid off for a single.
Floated in the line of the pads, Watling lunges forward to defend it.
Good length delivery outside off, de Grandhomme gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Full delivery into the stumps, Colin blocks it away.
Good length delivery outside off, Watling pushes it through covers for a single.
FOUR! Brilliant! Fuller delivery outside off, Watling drives it elegantly through the mid off region for a boundary. That was a top shot.

Rabada's unlucky! Brilliant delivery angling in from a length. Watling prods forward and goes for a drive. The ball sneaks in between the bat and the pad. Also misses the stumps. The batsman is really lucky there.
Short delivery into the body this time, Watling ducks under it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Tossed up outside off, de Grandhomme drives it straight back to the bowler.
Short into the stumps, de Grandhomme camps back and defends it.
Colin de Grandhomme is the new man in!

OUT! Maharaj gets his man! Full and fired wide outside off, Raval dances down track and tries to have a go at it. He misses it completely. Quinton gathers it and does not miss it this time. He quickly dislodges the bails and sends the batsman back to the hut. Raval's innings of sheer grit and determination comes to an end.
Floated up outside off, Raval prods forward and defends it.
That ball jumped and turned! Floated outside off and spinning in, Raval takes it on his body.
Length delivery outside off, Watling shoulders his arms at it.
The batsman has punched that ball through the offside.
That doesn't carry! Length delivery outside off, nips away a bit after pitching. Watling tries to defend it but he edges it. The ball falls short of the fielder at second slip. Lucky there!
Angling in from a length outside off, Watling covers his stumps and makes a brave leave.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Watling punches it wide of covers. Elgar scampers across and puts in a dive to stop the ball. Top class fielding.
Angling into the pads, Raval clips it fine down the leg side for a single.
Full outside off, Watling drives it through to mid off.
Spinning down leg, Watling prods forward to defend but gets an inside edge off the pads and just past short leg.
FOUR! Beautiful! Tossed up around off, Watling gets to the pitch of the ball and crisply drives it through the extra cover region for a boundary.
In the line of the stumps this time, Watling prods forward and defends it.
Tossed up outside off, Raval dances down the track and clips it through the mid-wicket region for a single. Brings up the 150 with it.
Floated outside off, Raval prods forward and defends it with an angled bat towards point.
Another bouncer from Rabada! Watling ducks under it.
Length delivery outside off, Watling goes for the drive on the up but misses it completely.
Short delivery again, Watling stands tall and defends it well.
Down the leg side again, Raval fends it towards backward square leg. They run a single.
Dug in short down the leg side, Raval ducks just in time to let that go through to the keeper.
Full delivery and Raval is behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Another full ball, Watling blocks it away.
Floated outside off, Watling lunges forward in defence.
Full delivery outside off, Watling drives this one towards covers.

Bye! This one went through everything! Quite full and spinning in, Raval prods forward in defence and gets beaten by the spin. The ball sneaks through between the bat and the pad. Luckily it just goes over the stumps and Quinton too cannot stop it. The ball runs away and the batsmen take a bye.
Tossed up around middle and off, Raval prods forward and defends it.
Floated outside off, this one does not turn. Raval tries to defend for the turn and gets beaten.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

DROPPED! Short delivery angling into the body, Raval rides the bounce and pulls that away. The ball goes straight towards the fielder at short mid-wicket. That did go like a rocket but Cook, present there stretched to his right however could not hold onto it. Another drop and Raval gets his third life. The ball runs away behind and the batsmen run a single.
This one is even further outside off, Raval shoulders his arms to it.
Rabada comes round the wicket this time, bowls it back of a length outside off. Raval watches the ball go through to the keeper.
Full toss outside off, Watling stays in his crease and pushes it down the ground for a triple through the mid off region. That was a poor delivery and he should have had put that away.
Good length delivery outside off, BJ Watling shuffles across and pushes it towards the cover fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman, presenting the full face of the bat.
Same shot, in the same area, same number of runs. Nicely done.
50-run stand between Raval and Watling!
Full on middle and leg, turning in, swept behind square on the leg side for a couple.
Darts this full around off, Raval presses forward to smother the spin.
Floats it up around off, steps out to this one and defends.
Full on off, defended off the front foot.
Keshav Maharaj to bowl from the other end.
A solid back foot defense from BJ Watling and that will be the end of the over.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Short one banged in, it's ducked and evaded.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Another one outside off, in the channel, another leave from Watling.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
The last session of play is about to get underway as Jeet Raval and BJ Watling stride out to the middle. Kagiso Rabada to start off with the ball.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Despite the resistance shown by the Black Caps, the Proteas are well on top of this game. Morne Morkel and Keshav Maharaj did all the damage with the pacer scalping 3 in total, looking as fearsome as ever, and the spinner bagging 2. The lead is just of 48 runs and the home side still has a lot of work to do. Join us for the final session of the day.

A solid fightback from New Zealand in the second half of this afternoon session. They were reduced to 90/5 in the first hour after play resumed, but then Jeet Raval and BJ Watling took things under their control and saw the session off without any further damage. The southpaw completed his fifty but is lucky to still be out there as he was given a couple of reprieves. 84 runs have been added in the session and the two are going along confidently.
Again down the leg side, Raval clips it fine but cannot get it past the fielder. THAT'S TEA ON DAY 3.
Way down the leg side, Raval clips it fine but the fielder at short fine leg stops it.
Full around off, Watling reaches out to it and drives it through the extra cover region. A single is taken.
A bit short this time but still outside off, Watling walks across and pushes it towards the fielder at mid off.
Sprayed down the leg side, Watling clips it through the square leg region for a single.
Floated outside off, Watling punches it through covers for a single.
Dug in short around off, Raval stays deep in his crease, hops and defends it to the ground.
Another delivery way outside off, Raval shoulders his arms to it.
Short delivery into the body, takes Raval by surprise. He somehow manages to pull it through the mid-wicket region for a couple.
Down the leg side this time, Raval only manages to clip it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Good length delivery angling into the stumps, Jeet stays deep in his crease and defends it.
Length delivery outside off, Raval gets an inside edge which thuds onto the pads.
Full on leg stump, angling down, Watling looks to sweep but misses.
Switches the angle and comes from over the wicket, it's flat and short outside off, BJ with a punch away on the off side.
Sliding in with the arm, worked away with the wrists behind square on the leg side for one.
Full delivery on the stumps, driven towards the mid on fielder. Won't get any run for it though.
Around the wicket to Raval, it's full on off, pushes away to the cover region.
Around the wicket to Raval, it's full on off, pushes away to the cover region.

Sharp bounce and a lot of movement for Rabada on that occasion. He hurls it outside off, it bites off the deck and swings in after going past BJ Watling. Good take by Quinton de Kock behind the stumps as he shuffles to his left to take it.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Watling mistimes the punch in front of covers.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Shortish and angling down leg, pulled fine down the leg side for a single.
Shaping across the left-hander, it's kept out solidly off the front foot with the full face of the bat.
Full ball on middle and off, Jeet Raval drives it back down and the fielder from mid off cuts it out.
Stays back to this one and it's darted on a length, defended.
Full around off, drilled back down to mid off by Watling.
layed to the point region by the batsman. Dot ball.
Flat, short and outside off from over the wicket, punched off the back foot for nothing.

THE CHANGE IN BOWLING ALMOST WORKS WONDERS! How has that missed? It's gone right through everything and everyone. You can see the frustration on Quinton de Kock's face as he knocks the bails off in anger. Some nice swerve for Duminy, Raval gives the charge and looks to go downtown. The ball goes right between bat and pad and past the leg stump as well. Quinton de Kock can't catch it as it goes behind. Doesn't reach the fence but three byes have been taken. Genuine chance goes begging!
From around the wicket, full outside off, blocked.
JP Duminy is introduced into the attack.
Down the leg side, Raval gloves it fine and picks up a single for doing so.
Outside off, short in length, Jeet looks to defend it away but misses.

Took Raval by surprise. But credit to the southpaw, he did very well to adjust. Banged in short, Jeet looks to pull initially, then backs out of it. Loses his balance in the process but well done in the end.
Angling across, on the shorter side of the length, left alone.
Slanting across on a back of a length, outside off, defended off the back foot by the southpaw.
FOUR! Hit that with authority! Short and into the body, Jeet Raval is on to it in a flash. Stands tall and muscles the pull through backward square leg for a boundary.
Kagiso Rabada is called back into the attack.
FOUR! Loose, poor line and Watling needs no second invitation to put it away. Down the leg side, he sweeps it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Turning away from outside off, no shot offered to that one.
Gives this a lot of air as it's looped outside off, Watling is a bit early into the drive as he mistimes it to covers.
Plants his front foot forward, gets to the pitch and dead-bats it.
Full around off, Jeet Raval comes down the track and whips it to mid-wicket. A misfield from skipper Faf du Plessis there allows the batsmen to take the run.
FOUR! Swept away! Lovely shot. Looped up on the stumps, Raval positions himself really early here. Kneels down and hits it through square leg to find the fence.

Just a few moments ago, Faf du Plessis had his fingers all black when he put his hand in the pocket. He then later realized that the heat bag in his pocket had broken. He even acted to throw it on umpire Rod Tucker who took it really sportingly and laughed it off. A good moment of fun on the field altogether.
More blocks, as expected from Watling, he drops this on the off side for nothing.
BJ Watling has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fuller length ball outside off, with excellent balance, the batsman pushes it out in front of covers.
Has a change of angle and comes over the wicket, Watling does extremely well here. He brings down a straight bat to this extremely full delivery and defends. Rock solid from the NZ keeper.
Back of a length and well outside off, a bit of width on offer which Jeet pounces on. Dabs it towards point and takes a single.
From around the wicket, Philander hurls it in the off stump channel, Jeet Raval as watchful as ever, lets it through.
Darts it quicker on off, BJ with a drive to mid off and that will be the end of the over.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Positions himself perfectly behind the line and meets it with a straight blade.
Risky from Raval! He skips down the track to this one and uppishly wrists it through the vacant mid on region. It rolls away down to long on as a single is taken.
Bowls it slower through the air, around off, Jeet Raval strides ahead and pushes it back down the track.
Excellent delivery! Full and darted outside off, Raval leaves it alone.
Angling in on middle and leg, Raval tucks it past the mid-wicket fielder and picks up a single for doing so.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off on a good length, Raval covers the line well and carefully lets it be.

Lovely timing. Excellent use of the wrists from BJ Watling. He leans across and flicks this full ball between mid on and mid-wicket. It won't go all the way to the fence but it's enough to fetch him three good runs.
Full ball attacking the stumps, BJ Watling stays behind the line and defends.
Full ball attacking the stumps, BJ Watling stays behind the line and defends.
Dragged short this time, Raval camps back and punches this one towards covers.
Short delivery outside off, Raval goes to cut it through the point region but fails to make contact.
Short ball down the leg side, Watling clips it through the square leg region for a single.
Floated outside off, Watling lunges forward and defends it in front of the fielder at silly point.
Full into the stumps, Watling digs it out as he ends up pushing it towards the bowler.
Floated around off, Watling prods forward and defends it back to the bowler.
Coming in on middle and leg, worked away on the on side for nothing.
Connects well this time but is unfortunate to find the fielder. Jeet leans ahead and firmly drives it straight to the extra cover fielder.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Short and outside off, Raval hangs back and drops it on the off side.
Loose from Jeet Raval on this occasion. It's on a fuller length and well outside off, he goes for the expansive drive through the covers but misses.
Length delivery outside off, plays it off the edge towards the slip cordon.
Back to around the wicket, defended off the front foot.
Loopy well outside off, Raval reaches out to it and off the inside half wrists it past the short leg fielder towards mid-wicket. A single is taken but that was a bit risky.
Flat, short and outside off, keeps a bit low too as Jeet off his back foot pushes it past silly point.
Over the wicket now, stays right behind the line and defends this one out.
Drifting in from around off on a fuller length, Watling with a solid push through the covers for a single.
From around the wicket, it's tossed up on off, Watling lunges ahead to block.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Bit fuller in the channel outside off, Raval reaches out to drive it away from his body but is beaten past the outside edge.
Length delivery outside off, left alone.

That's dropped! You don't really expect that from one of the best fielders in the side. Was a pretty straightforward one, should have taken it. Back of a length from around the wicket, coming in, cramps Raval for room as he cuts this away. It's straight to Duminy at gully who spills it after crouching low to take it. Jeet Raval survives, can he make the most of it?

An edge which falls well short. Back of a length delivery outside off, Watling hangs his bat out to it and gets an edge which falls well short of Faf du Plessis at second slip. It goes through him and a single is taken.
Length delivery just around off, defended off the front foot by the batsman.

Time for drinks! South Africa on the ascendancy as half the Kiwi side is back in the hut. The hosts are in deep trouble here and the current pair of Raval and Watling have an everest of a task ahead of them. A lot hinges on these two. The wicket has shown that if you dig in, runs are there for you.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short delivery into the stumps, Raval camps back and defends it.
Straighter one this time outside off, Raval plays for the spin and fails to make contact. Quinton de Kock was quick to gather it and dislodge the bails.
Fuller this time, Raval drives it back to the bowler.
Raval gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Loopy delivery outside off, Raval prods forward to defend but the ball runs off the outside edge through the slip cordon for a couple.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Watling punches it for a couple through covers.
Watling prods forward and defends it.
4th Test fifty for Jeet Raval!

Fifty for Raval! Good length delivery outside off, Raval lunges forward and pushes it through the gap between point and cover for a triple. It has been a fine knock till now, he will want to build on the momentum and make it big.
Full delivery angling into the stumps, Raval shuffles across and prods forward to defend it.
In the line of the stumps, Raval pushes this one towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
Angling into the stumps, Raval stays in his crease and defends it.
Vernon Philander is called back into the attack.
Watling gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it towards the fielder at mid off.
Loopy delivery in the line of the stumps, Watling lunges forward to defend it.
Quicker one outside off, left alone.
Tossed up on the stumps, Watling prods forward and defends it.
Another full delivery in the line of the stumps, Watling pushes it back to the bowler.
Full on the pads, Watling clips it towards the fielder at mid-wicket.
On the pads, Raval clips it towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length delivery into the stumps, Raval pushes it back to the bowler. Morkel has a shy at the striker's end but misses.
Fuller delivery this time, Raval drives this one through covers for a couple.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Pierced! Good length delivery outside off, Raval opens the face of his bat and guides it through the third man region for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off, Raval cuts it past point for a couple. New Zealand now lead by a run.
BJ Watling is in next to bat.

OUT! Neesham throws it away! Tossed up around off, Jimmy dances down the track and goes for the big slog but only manages to find the fielder at short mid-wicket. Skipper Faf du Plessis hangs himself in the air and plucks it off to take a stunning catch. Maharaj is making it count. New Zealand still trail by a run.
Neesham gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
FOUR! Neesham gives it a fitting reply! Tossed up in the line of the stumps, Neesham sweeps it hard through the mid-wicket region for a boundary.

Shout for LBW! Spinning in from outside off, that one did spin a lot from the rough. Neesham comes way across to defend it but gets hit on his pads. The players appeal but the umpire stays put. The impact was surely outside off.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads.
Jimmy Neesham in the new man in for New Zealand.

OUT! Dragged it on! Floated way outside off, Nicholls reaches out to it and goes for the sweep. Cannot make the desired contact as he gets an inside edge which ricochets into the stumps. Such a poor shot to get out on. He was disappointed and should be. The centurion of the first innings hardly made any difference. Keshav Maharaj gets his first.
Henry Nicholls is getting some treatment on his left forearm after suffering some blows there.
Way outside off this time, left alone. Expensive over from Morkel. 15 runs off it.
Nicholls pulls it away towards the deep mid-wicket fielder for a single.
Another short one this time, Raval pulls this one towards the fielder at deep square leg for a single.
Raval stays in his crease and defends it well.

Five Wides! Tries to put in some extra effort and ends up bowling even more short as the batsman looks to pull it away. Even the keeper cannot reach it as it was too high for him. The ball races away to the boundary.
FOUR! Good shot! Another one to follow! Another short delivery and Raval pulls this away for a boundary through the backward square leg region. This one pierced all the gaps.
FOUR! Top shot! Short ball into the batsman, Raval takes on the bouncer this time and pulls it through the mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Way wide outside off, the batsman tries to pad it away but it was still far from him.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Raval drives it through the covers for a single.
The batsman has driven it through mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated in the line of the stumps, Nicholls sweeps it through the square leg region for a single.
Another short ball into the batsman, Raval misses his pull this time and gets an edge on it which then goes onto hit the helmet.
Nearly does the trick for Morkel! Short delivery into the body, Nicholls hops again and tries to defend. Gets hit on his glove and the ball flies towards short fine leg for a single.
Back of a length delivery bowled across, Nicholls pushes this one towards the fielder at point.
Another short delivery angling across, Nicholls gets behind the line of the ball and defends it well.
Replay of the previous delivery. Nothing different at all.
Short delivery again to Nicholls from Morkel, the batsman hops and defends it in front of the fielder at short leg.
Raval gets behind the line of the ball and defends it on the off side.
Full outside off, Raval dances down the track and drives this one towards extra cover.
Floated outside off, Raval leans forward and defends it.
Floated around off, Nicholls sweeps this one through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Nicholls lunges to the pitch of the ball and drives it towards covers.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Nicholls pushes it towards covers and calls for a quick single. His partner responds well to it.
Short delivery again, Nicholls this time manages to work it through the leg side for a couple.
Another one outside off, the batsman chooses to let it through to the keeper.
Length delivery angling across from a length, left alone.
Another short delivery which rises a bit more from the deck. Nicholls stands tall and defends it off his gloves.
Length delivery outside off, Nicholls shoulders his arms to it.

First signs of spin! Spinning in from outside off, Raval stays deep in his crease and tries to cut it. But ends up getting a thick inside edge into the ground. Luckily that did not go onto hit the stumps.
Way outside off this time, left alone.
Flighted outside off, Raval gets to the pitch of the ball to defend it.
In the line of the stumps, Raval gets behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Floated outside off, Raval pushes this one towards point.
Tossed up outside off, Raval stays on his back foot and pushes it back to the bowler.
Nasty! Short delivery into the body, the batsman tries to sway away from the line of the ball but fails to do so as he gets hit on his arm pit.
Way outside off, left alone.
Henry Nicholls, the centurion from the first innings, is the next man in. Walks in once again in a tricky situation, NZ are going to need him to come good again.

OUT! Morne Morkel strikes in his very first over after break! Length delivery angling in and then nips away after pitching. Broom prods forward in defence and tries to push at it but he gets beaten by the away movement as he nicks it. The ball flies away behind and Quinton de Kock stretches to his right to take a brilliant catch. Another wicket falls and NZ are in trouble.
Another length delivery outside off, Raval guides it towards third man to get a single.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Cross seamed delivery pitched short, Raval camps back and hooks it through the square leg region for a boundary. A totally different approach to this session it seems.
FOUR! Width and punished! Good length delivery outside off, Raval stays in his crease and cuts it through the gully region for a boundary.
Morne Morkel will bowl from the other end.
Down the leg side, Broom tries to clip it but fails to make contact.
Tossed up outside off, Broom defends it in front of the fielder at silly point.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

We are back for the afternoon session. A fine, fine two hours await if the first session is anything to go by. Testing period for both teams, could dictate how the match goes. Will be Jeet Raval and Neil Broom to continue with Keshav Maharaj to start things off with the ball.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

New Zealand still have a long task ahead as they still trail by 36 runs. If the first two days are anything to go by, the pitch will become batting friendly which would excite the Kiwis. Should be an exciting second session as well. Join us in a short while.

A fantastic first session of cricket where we have seen a fierce contest between the bat and ball! After losing two early wickets of Latham and Williamson, the Kiwis were put on the back foot really early but the grit shown from Raval and Broom was commendable as they saw the session through without any further inroads. The South African pacers were right on the money from the very first ball and kept on building pressure from both the ends by bowling probing lengths. But they weren't awarded duly. Rabada and Philander both bowled fiercely but weren't rewarded as compared to Morkel who scalped two.
Ripping bouncer just outside off, Jeet Raval drops his hands and evades it. A testing first session for New Zealand has come to an end. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 3!

Man... That's just flown by! This is monstrous bowling from Kagiso Rabada. Pounds it in on a back of a length, it's just around off and there's some venomous bounce on that. Rises onto Raval really quickly and goes off the shoulder of the bat. Flies past the silly point fielder and rolls to point.
BANG! There it is! Kagiso Rabada on the money. Fires it in full going for the yorker but ends up bowling a low full toss, it's still accurate as Raval digs it out on the leg side.

Jeet Raval's gloves have taken more of a beating than Quinton de Kock's today. Brutal but he's up for it. Short on off, he takes the bottom hand off to fend it away on the off side. Gets it off the glove as it falls safely.
Angling in at first but then it's going away, Raval is watchful as he lets it go past him.
Coming in on a back of a length, very close to the off pole, Raval with the full face of the bat defends it on the off side.
Tossed up on the stumps, more of the same from Neil Broom. Another strong block.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated on off, Neil brings his bat ahead of his pad and presents a tight defensive shot.
Fuller and served outside off, blocked.
Drifting in from around off, Broom comes ahead and gets it off the inner half as he attempts to defend.
Full ball attacking the stumps, Broom dead-bats it into the track.
He's being tested here but is rising up to the challenge, both literally and figuratively. Short one on the body, blocked well short of Cook at short leg.
Short and angling in, sharp bounce off the deck, Raval rides the bounce and defends it down.
Stephen Cook is positioned now at short leg. Expect the short ones to be bombed at Jeet Raval.
Another one with steep bounce, on middle and leg, Raval fends it down on the track.

Oh that's nicely played. You need sound technique to play those kind of deliveries. Short of a length, crouched initially but then rose to defend it down on the track. Took his bottom hand off at the last second while doing so.
Outside off and it's zipping off the deck, left alone by Raval.
Rabada comes steaming in and at 140 clicks, angles it in on off, Jeet Raval leans ahead and buries it into the track.
Tossed up from Maharaj, Neil with a stride ahead to defend and that will be the end of the over.
Floats it up on middle and off, Broom meets it with the full face of the bat.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off on a flatter trajectory, played to point.
Drifting in from around off, a solid front foot defense to keep it out.
Full outside off, driven to covers. Straight to the fielder so no run is taken.
Further outside off, easier for Raval to let it be.
Outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Outside off on a good length, left alone for the keeper to collect.

FOUR! Shot. Slightly loose and Jeet Raval puts it away. Length delivery outside off, it's driven square of the wicket past point for a boundary. Just goes to show, if you stick around for a while on this track, you can get your shots away. The ball is getting a little soft as well which will allow the batsmen to play more freely.
Bit fullish in length from Kagiso Rabada, hurls it outside off, Raval taps it away to the cover region.
Angling in from a good length, on off, Raval with a good block to keep it out.
FOUR! One loose ball and it's punished. Down the leg side, Neil Broom kneels and sweeps it behind backward square leg to end the over with a boundary.
Some nice drift on this from Maharaj, draws the batsman forward to defend.
Coming in with the angle on a flatter trajectory, flicked away past short leg. No run taken by the batsmen.
A full toss drifting in on middle and off, worked away to mid-wicket.
Flighted ball landed just around off, Neil Broom comes ahead and blocks.

Starts off from around the wicket and tosses it up on the stumps, Broom with a lunge forward to block but is caught on the pads. An appeal from the keeper and the bowler but the umpire remains unmoved. Seems there was an inside edge, maybe going down leg as well.
As expected, spin has been introduced as Keshav Maharav marks his run up to bowl his first over of the day. Has a slip and a short leg in place.
Jeet Raval shoulders his arms and lets the last ball of the over go by.
Pitched fractionally ahead of a length, outside off, pushed to the covers for nought.

Beaten! Served just outside off, holding its line, beats the outside edge on the attempted poke. Rabada has been hitting the right lines from ball no.1 and bowling at great pace. Finding his rhythm perfectly here.
Quinton runs back to the fence behind him to get his helmet. A rare sight to see the keeper run all the way in the middle of the over. Seems like spin might be introduced.
Nicely dealt with by Jeet Raval. It's angling back in to him on a back of a length, he stands tall and fends it away down on the leg side.

Rabada switches the angle and comes from around the wicket, hurls it on an excellent length just outside off, Raval leaves it alone. That zipped off the surface as de Kock collected it at a good height.
Fuller length delivery attacking the stumps, driven towards mid on. Dot ball.
Short and into the body, Raval pulls it to the left of the mid-wicket fielder for a single.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Angling across, harmless really, easy leave for Jeet.
Sprays it on the pads, worked away behind square on the leg side for a single.
Coming back into Neil Broom, on a back of a length, he's expecting this and deals with it well. Tucks it to mid-wicket for no run.
Morkel goes short and keeps it around off, punched away a bit square on the off side.
Morne Morkel is called back into the attack.
Curling back in on middle and leg, Broom tucks it to mid-wicket and takes a single to keep strike.
Full and tailing back in from outside off, Neil Broom looking confident here now. Presses forward and defends it with the full face of the bat.
Kicking off the deck outside off, Broom rises with the bounce and steers it to point.
Fuller length delivery outside off, solidly pushed out off the front foot.
FOUR! Nicely done. Outside off on a back of a length, Broom with an angled bat plays this very late. Runs it past the gully fielder and sends it across the third man fence.

In the air... But it's safe! Raval had no idea about that, Rabada with a sharp one. At 142.3 kph, he bangs it in short on middle and leg, rises quickly on Raval who awkwardly plays at this. It goes off the edge and falls safely behind square on the leg side. A single is taken.
Testing over from Philander comes to an end. Brings the last ball back in, Neil stands firm and blocks it out.
Squares up the batsman with the movement, angles in at first, moves away at the last second and takes the outside edge. Goes towards the diving gully fielder. No run taken.

FOUR! Shot. This time he gets it in the gap. Back of a length outside off and it's through the gap in the covers. Bavuma tries chasing it down, puts in a slide but gets stuck as he stretches his right hand out to stop it. Boundary for Broom.
Shortish delivery outside off, Neil with a powerful punch but it's straight to the point fielder. Unfortunate on that occasion, got that right off the meat of the bat.
Curling on a shorter length, from around off, Broom punches it behind square on the off side. Beats the gully fielder and picks up a couple of runs.

Look at that... another beaut from Vernon Philander! Neil Broom must be sweating bullets out there, even in this weather. Not the easiest of things to stand up against Philander when he's on song like this. Back of a length moving away late around off, beats the outside edge and goes to the keeper. Broom wanted to push it away but missed.
Outside off, length delivery from Raval, it's dabbed to point with an open face.
Marginally ahead of a length, easy enough for the batsman to push it in front of covers.
Slanting across just outside off, holds its line as Jeet Raval leaves it alone. Ensured that he covered the line and didn't have any damage done.
Brings it in closer to the off stick and hits the deck on a back of a length, Raval moves across a touch and defends it down in front of point.
On a nice length this time, shaping across once more, another leave by the left-hander.
Angling across on a back of a length, well outside off, left alone comfortably.

Absolute ripper from Philander to end the over. He's left there standing with his hand on his face as to how that's missed. Length delivery angling in on off, it moves away and squares Broom up. It's too good for him, a little more than it should have really. Just about beats the outside edge and thuds into Quinton de Kock's gloves.
In the corridor of uncertainty, a good leave from the batsman.
Moving away from Neil Broom on a back of a length, he covers the line well and lets it be.
Lovely placement. Coming in on middle and leg, Broom picks it off his pads and flicks it nicely through square leg for a couple of runs.
Back of a length around off, Broom moves across a step and works it in front of mid-wicket.

It's pitched, it's seamed and that's everything a bowler could hope for. Vernon Philander will feel unlucky he's not got anything out of that. Full around off and swinging away late after pitching, Neil Broom looks to drive it back down the ground but is beaten hands down. Nothing he could have done about that, though.
Drinks break!
Short delivery into the body, Raval stands tall and defends it off his glove.
Down the leg side, Broom clips it towards square leg for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Broom stays in his crease and pushes it towards point.
Again way down the leg side, Raval tries to flicks it off his pads but misses. The ball hits the pads and goes towards fine leg for a leg bye.
Down the leg side on a length, Raval clips it fine for a couple.
Fuller delivery on the pads, Raval clips this one towards mid-wicket. The fielder there dives to his left to stop it.
Kagiso Rabada is brought into the bowling attack.
Fuller delivery outside off, nipping away. Broom gets this one towards point off the outer half of his bat.
Good length delivery around off, Broom pushes this one towards the fielder at point.
Absolute ripper this time! Good length delivery outside off, nips away after pitching. Broom stays in his crease and tries to poke at it but luckily the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Fuller around off this time, Broom stays in his crease and defends it.
Philander seems to get some movement off the deck now as this one nips away after pitching on a length outside off. Broom stays in his crease and watches it through.
Good length delivery angling away from around off, Broom gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Down the leg side, Raval fends it in front of the fielder at short leg.
Good length delivery around off, nips in after pitching. Raval covers his stumps and lets it go through to the keeper.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length delivery outside off, Broom guides it for a single through point and gets the first run of his Test career. The crowd applauds for the debutant.
Dug in short this time, Broom ducks under it to evade it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Way down the leg side, Raval tries to clip it but fails to make contact.
Back of a length delivery down the leg side, Raval tries to clip it but misses. He gets hit high on his thigh pad.
Down the leg side, Raval defends it towards mid-wicket.
Interesting fielding change here. A short cover and a very close-in silly mid off are in place.

LOUD SHOUT FOR A LEG BEFORE! Turned down, however. Length delivery angling into the stumps, Raval lunges forward in defence and luckily manages to find a bat to it. The players appeal but the umpire says no. He gets an inside edge onto his pads which saves him from being dead plum.
Good length delivery outside off, Raval camps back and defends it towards mid off.
Length delivery outside off, Raval prods forward and defends it.
Big ask of Neil Broom. He's walked into the heat of the battle and this will be a real test of his abilities.
Broom gets a warm welcome from Morkel who digs it short the very first ball. The batsman manages to duck under it.

OUT! HUGE WICKET FOR SA! Good length delivery around off, Kane Williamson stays in his crease and tries to defend it. The ball whizzes past the outside edge and goes straight into the gloves of the keeper. The South Africans go up in appeal and Kumar Dharmasena says no. The Proteas seem confident as they go for a review the very next moment. Replays show that it was a fair delivery. Then the umpire calls for the HotSpot which shows there was a very faint edge which the South Africans recognized really well. The umpire has to change his decision and the New Zealand skipper has to walk back to the pavilion. Morkel has got the main wicket and he will be delighted with his bowling today.
Big, big moment in the game, this! South Africa have taken a review for a caught behind decision against Kane Williamson. Over to the third umpire Bruce Oxenford now...
Length delivery outside off, Williamson lunges forward to reach the pitch of the ball to defend it.
Length delivery outside off, Raval uses his crease and defends it on the off side. Calls for a quick single and his partner responds well as they complete it easily.
Good length delivery outside off, Raval defends this one through to point.
Back of a length delivery angling into the body, Williamson camps back and pushes it towards mid on for a quick single.

Spills this down the leg side, Jeet looks to flick but misses. Quinton de Kock dives to his right to stop it and gets a glove on it, two byes are taken as he ball thuds off his glove a little away from him.

FOUR! Shot! Overpitched and it's been put away. Full and swinging in, just outside off, Raval with an excellent straight bat leans into the shot and drives it straight back down the ground for a boundary.
Shaping away a shade from around off, takes the outside edge of Jeet Raval's bat as he tries to feel for it. It goes past the narrow gully fielder and two runs are taken.
Beautiful. The line is such from Philander that it's making the batsman play. Pounds this on a back of a length, just around off, it's defended down on the track from the crease.
Just back of a length, on middle and leg, Raval goes back and tucks it away on the leg side.
Back of a length delivery on off, really tight line from Vernon Philander, Jeet Raval stays perfectly behind the line and meets it with a straight blade.
Outside off, left alone.
Angling into the stumps, Williamson stays in his crease and defends it.
Good length delivery which kicks off the surface and nips in a bit. Williamson covers his stumps and lets it through to the keeper.
Kane Williamson is the next batsman in.

OUT! Morkel draws first blood! Latham's poor run of form continues with this! Fuller length delivery angling away from outside off, Latham goes for a drive on the up. He manages to edge it, which flies towards the slip region. Duminy at fourth slip makes no mistake and gobbles it safely. The constant length around off has helped Morkel get his man. Another poor start for New Zealand.
Angling across from a length, Latham lunges forward and shoulders his arms to it.
Down the leg side, Raval flicks it fine for a single towards fine leg.
Length delivery around off, Latham covers his stumps and pushes it towards mid-wicket.
Philander has a bit of problem with the ball. He shows it to the umpire who chops off the extra threading.
Back of a length delivery down the leg side, Latham shuffles across a bit and clips it through the square leg region for a couple.
Fuller delivery way outside off, Latham leans into it and lets it go through to the keeper.
Length delivery angled around off, Latham shuffles across and fends it on the leg side.
Similar line and length this time, Latham prods forward and pushes this one on the off side.
Length delivery outside off, Latham gets behind the line of the ball to defend it.
Down the leg side, Raval tries to clip it on the leg side but fails to make contact.
FOUR BYES! Another short one to Raval, this one flew off the deck. Raval somehow managed to duck under it as the ball flew over him, then over the keeper for a boundary.
Shorter in length, Raval sways away from the line of the delivery to let it through to the keeper..
FOUR! Another lucky boundary! Back of a length delivery angling across, Raval rides the bounce and tries to defend it but gets a thick outside edge which flies through the slip cordon for a boundary.
Another short one to follow, seems like the length for Raval from Morkel. Raval covers his stumps and shoulders his arms to it.
Short delivery to start with this time, angling across. Raval stays in his crease and lets it through to the keeper.
Length delivery around off, Tom Latham takes a confident stride forward and blocks it in front of point.
Coming back in on a back of a length, it's tucked to the vacant area at backward square leg for a comfortable single.
In two minds is Jeet Raval. He decides to leave this very late, ends up edging it behind towards the slip cordon. Luckily, it went along the ground.
Outside off once more, going across the batsman this time, it's left alone.
Bowls it around off, tails it back in slightly, Raval judges it well and shoulders his arms to it.
Jagging back in on a good length from around off, Philander on target straightaway. Raval covers the line and defends well.
Vernon Philander will bowl from the other end.

NOT OUT! Yes there was an inside edge which saved him! South Africa have lost a review there! Length delivery angling into the stumps, Tom Latham prods forward in defence. It hits the pads and goes towards the gully fielder. The players appeal and the umpire says no. Faf and Morkel decide to go for the review for an LBW appeal. Replays show that there was an inside edge which means Latham is safe and the umpire got it right. Close call, was just a faint edge so difficult to tell really.

A review from South Africa! Tom Latham has been caught leg before and given not out. Faf du Plessis instantly signals to take it upstairs. Latham however remains confident that he's safe. Inside edge maybe?
FOUR! Lucky runs to start with! Full delivery in the line of the stumps, Latham prods forward in defence, the ball catches the outside edge and runs through the slip cordon for a boundary.
Good length delivery outside off, Latham stays undisturbed in his crease.
Third leave in a row this time. Latham does not need to play at those which are darted way outside off.
A bit back of a length this time, around off, Latham stays in his crease and shoulders his arms to it.
Way wide outside off to start with from Morkel, no movement there this time. Latham lets it go through to the keeper.
